<description>
Currently the GetTransaction return value is a nullable transaction
pointer, where nullptr represents two different outcomes: I/O error and
missing tx.

Reporting a confirmed transaction as missing is wrong, so properly
return an error instead.
</description>

Force pushed to re-create the patch from scratch (addressing all feedback + "rebase")

<!--

• Found two correctness issues and several wording problems.

  - [P2] src/index/txindex.cpp:187: iterator failures still become nullopt. A LevelDB iterator I/O error makes Valid() false, while malformed key data makes GetKey() false. Both terminate the loop and can still produce
    “transaction not found.” Thus fadc37c does not fully establish the contract claimed by its message.

  - [P2] src/index/txindex.cpp:197: the two explicit continue branches also preserve false negatives. A missing block-index entry or missing BLOCK_HAVE_DATA is described as corruption/incomplete persistence, but if no later
    candidate succeeds, FindTx returns nullopt. A better pattern is to remember the inconsistency, continue searching for hash-prefix collisions/duplicate transactions, and throw if no valid match is ultimately found.

Concept ACK

- [x] fa5ad60c32 introduced `test_getrawtransaction_block_data_errors` showing default errors when the block is not available and when the block cannot be read
- [x] fa5b2f13da `getrawtransaction` no longer checks the block availability inline, task delegated to `CheckBlockDataAvailability`, now I/O errors can be detected in `GetTransaction` and thrown
- [x] fa8a5b033b introduced `feature_io_errors.py` to test I/O errors, creates a psbt and makes the block file unavailable, showing default behavior when rpc commands try to read this file
- [x] 3333a91dbf `FindTx` still returns nullopt for a missing tx, but on the I/O and index, errors are handled here, we now log the warning and throw instead of continuing (updated test to use the change)
- [x] faa4bb35ae In `ProcessPSBT` now using `GetTransaction` instead of a more verbose tx lookup

Changes look good to me, left a few nits, I do have a question though;

I wonder if throwing immediately here could prevent callers from trying other lookups that might still succeed for example in `ProcessPSBT`, we first call `GetTransaction` which checks the mempool and txindex, if the tx isnt found we use `FindCoins` to look in the utxo set

But if `FindTx` throws, we never reach that last check, even though the utxo set might still have the input information.
[2026-10-14] c:6169950150 comment by maflcko (member):
[quoted text omitted]

Correct. But this is intentional: I'd say if someone is running with a corrupt index (or an index with stale data from an unclean shutdown, it would be good to notify them about it as early as possible. This way, they can either disable the index, or recreate it by deleting the index folder. Somehow adding extra fallback code means they'll still run into the issue, just later.
